target.title: fix(nvidia): sync recommended models with featured catalog
target.body:
## Summary

Keeps OpenClaw's recommended NVIDIA Endpoint models aligned with NVIDIA's authoritative featured-model catalog instead of leaving users with stale recommendations. The bundled fallback and provider documentation now match NVIDIA's current five featured models, while authenticated setup and model-selection paths continue pulling the live catalog from NVIDIA's static JSON feed.

### What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where NVIDIA Endpoint users could see outdated recommended models and metadata after NVIDIA updated its featured catalog.

## Changes

- Refresh the bundled NVIDIA fallback with Nemotron 3 Ultra, Nemotron 3 Super, GLM 5.2, Kimi K2.6, and Minimax M3 using the values from NVIDIA's featured-model JSON.
- Retain previously shipped model refs as deprecated compatibility rows with current replacements.
- Update the NVIDIA provider documentation to match the authoritative catalog.
- Extend NVIDIA catalog, onboarding, and registration tests for the refreshed rows.

### Why This Change Was Made

NVIDIA's public `featured-models.json` is the source of truth for current recommendations. OpenClaw already fetches that feed for authenticated setup and model selection; this change also aligns the bundled unavailable-feed fallback and documentation with the same source.

## Validation

### Evidence

- Live equality check against `https://assets.ngc.nvidia.com/products/api-catalog/featured-models.json` passed for all five expected rows and their context/max-output metadata.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/nvidia/provider-catalog.test.ts extensions/nvidia/index.test.ts extensions/nvidia/onboard.test.ts` — 27 tests passed.
- `corepack pnpm docs:check-mdx` — passed.
- `corepack pnpm docs:check-links` — 5,544 internal links checked, 0 broken.
- `corepack pnpm format:docs:check` — passed.
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` — passed.

## Notes

### User Impact

New NVIDIA setup and model-selection flows show the current featured models from NVIDIA's live catalog. If that feed is unavailable, the bundled fallback now presents the same current recommendations while older configured model refs remain resolvable.

Related: https://github.com/NVIDIA-dev/openclaw-tracking/issues/817
